item.text:
Using the local prior as the factual base. I did not re-fetch the structured country-year indicators you already supplied, and I did not use the client matrix.

**Office, Authority, Constraints**
- Prayut Chan-o-cha was Thailand’s prime minister in 2022 and also held the defense portfolio during the July censure debate, so he had executive authority over the cabinet and security apparatus, but not unchecked control over parliament or the courts.
- His authority was materially constrained by the 2017 constitution, coalition arithmetic in the House, and the Constitutional Court’s term-limit case.
- On **August 24, 2022**, the court suspended him from active duties while it reviewed the eight-year term-limit petition; deputy prime minister Prawit Wongsuwan acted in his place.
- On **September 30, 2022**, the court ruled he could continue in office, using the 2017 constitution’s effective date as the start point for the eight-year clock.
- Inference from that sequence: actions between **August 24 and September 29, 2022** should be attributed to the acting PM/cabinet, not Prayut personally.

**Retained Sources**
- [General Prayut Chan-o-cha, Thailand’s APEC 2022 statement](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/apecpmstatement-021065-2) - Ministry of Foreign Affairs, **February 10, 2022**. Precise fact: he publicly set the 2022 APEC frame around post-COVID recovery and the BCG model, which confirms he was still actively exercising PM-level agenda-setting early in 2022. Period fit: very strong for the year’s opening policy narrative. Attribution: direct ruler statement. Limitations: self-presenting, programmatic, and promotional. Contrary points: later protests and court intervention show the agenda was contested and politically fragile.

- [The 14th session of the 25th House of Representatives meeting](https://web.parliament.go.th/view/7/%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A2%E0%B8%A5%E0%B8%B0%E0%B9%80%E0%B8%AD%E0%B8%B5%E0%B8%A2%E0%B8%94%E0%B8%82%E0%B9%88%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A7_EN/news%20%E0%B8%82%E0%B9%88%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A7%E0%B8%9B%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%B0%E0%B8%8A%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%AA%E0%B8%B1%E0%B8%A1%E0%B8%9E%E0%B8%B1%E0%B8%99%E0%B8%98%E0%B9%8C/1136/EN-US) - House of Representatives of Thailand, **July 23, 2022**. Precise fact: Prayut, as prime minister and defense minister, survived the censure vote, with **256 confidence votes, 206 no-confidence votes, and 9 abstentions**. Period fit: strong mid-year political checkpoint. Attribution: direct parliamentary record. Limitations: this measures legislative survival, not popular approval or policy quality. Contrary points: the vote still exposed coalition dependence and looming instability.

- [ศาลรัฐธรรมนูญรับคำร้อง "8 ปี ประยุทธ์" สั่งหยุดปฏิบัติหน้าที่](https://www.thaipbs.or.th/news/content/318741) - Thai PBS, **August 24, 2022**. Precise fact: the Constitutional Court unanimously accepted the petition and, by **5-4**, ordered Prayut to suspend active duties pending a ruling. Period fit: essential for the office/authority timeline. Attribution: direct reporting on the court action. Limitations: a news report, not the judgment text itself. Contrary points: the later September ruling reversed the practical effect of this suspension.

- [ข่าวที่ ๒๒/๒๕๖๕ วันที่ ๓๐ กันยายน ๒๕๖๕](https://www.constitutionalcourt.or.th/th/library_occ/more_news.php?cid=923&gr=0&kword=&ldate=&nid=0&offset=10&sdate=&startoffset=0) - Constitutional Court of Thailand, **September 30, 2022**. Precise fact: the official court notice identifies the eight-year-term case against Prayut and the court’s consideration of whether his premiership had ended under the constitution. Period fit: primary legal anchor for the end-of-September decision. Attribution: official court record. Limitations: the search-result text is terse; for outcome detail I paired it with Thai PBS below. Contrary points: the same case ended with a stay-in-office ruling rather than removal.

- [มติศาลรัฐธรรมนูญเสียงข้างมาก ชี้ "ประยุทธ์" เป็นนายกฯยังไม่ครบ 8 ปี](https://www.thaipbs.or.th/news/content/320025) - Thai PBS, **September 30, 2022**. Precise fact: the court’s majority held that Prayut had not yet served eight years, with the count starting from **April 6, 2017**. Period fit: strongest legal-resolution source for the year. Attribution: direct reporting of the verdict and rationale. Limitations: still a report, not the full written opinion. Contrary points: opposition arguments counted from 2014 and would have ended his tenure in August 2022.

- [Thailand: 2022 Article IV Consultation](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2022/09/16/thailand-2022-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-and-statement-by-the-523532) - IMF, **September 16, 2022**. Precise fact: Thailand’s economy was recovering but unevenly, with **rapidly rising inflation driven by energy prices** and downside risks dominating the outlook. Period fit: strong inherited-conditions source for economic context. Attribution: multilateral, independent macro assessment. Limitations: national-level economic context, not ruler-specific causality. Contrary points: it also recognizes policy space and recovery momentum, so it is not purely negative.

- [Thailand’s Economy Remains Resilient amid Global Headwinds](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2022/12/14/thailand-s-economy-remains-resilient-amid-global-headwinds) - World Bank, **December 14, 2022**. Precise fact: the Bank projected **3.4% growth in 2022**, but also flagged elevated inflation and a projected rise in poverty as relief measures faded. Period fit: excellent year-end economic wrap-up. Attribution: independent development institution. Limitations: country macro picture, not personal ruler performance. Contrary points: the report also emphasizes tourism recovery and resilience, so it supports both constraint and partial recovery narratives.

- [Thailand: Rights Repressed](https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/01/12/thailand-rights-repressed) - Human Rights Watch, **January 12, 2023**. Precise fact: HRW says the Prayut الحكومة pursued politically motivated prosecutions and repression across **2022**, which is directly relevant to Chapters 3B and 4B. Period fit: strong retrospective rights synthesis. Attribution: independent critical rights source. Limitations: advocacy framing, though well documented. Contrary points: the report is broad and does not isolate every act to Prayut personally.

- [Thailand: Police Forcibly Disperse APEC Protesters](https://www.hrw.org/news/2022/11/22/thailand-police-forcibly-disperse-apec-protesters) - Human Rights Watch, **November 22, 2022**. Precise fact: HRW documented police beatings and rubber-bullet use against largely peaceful APEC protesters in Bangkok. Period fit: very strong for late-2022 protest repression. Attribution: directly tied to the Prayut government. Limitations: focuses on one protest episode, not the whole year. Contrary points: officials portrayed the dispersal as crowd-control/self-defense, so the episode is contested.

- [กสม.แถลงประเด็นเจ้าหน้าที่รัฐละเมิดสิทธิเสรีภาพผู้ชุมนุม สื่อมวลชน และผู้พิการ](https://prachatai.com/journal/2022/09/100323) - Prachatai, **September 1, 2022**. Precise fact: the National Human Rights Commission said police action against peaceful protesters was an excessive interference with rights, and it also criticized restrictions affecting media freedom. Period fit: strong Thai-language critical source for Chapter 3B/4B. Attribution: local-language, independent, critical. Limitations: reports on an NHRC statement, not a direct court finding. Contrary points: the government could argue the measures were lawful crowd control.

- [Permanent Secretary for Foreign Affairs reaffirmed Thailand’s commitment towards the achievement of a World Free of Nuclear Weapons](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/tpnw2022-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) - Ministry of Foreign Affairs, **June 28, 2022**. Precise fact: Thailand reaffirmed support for a world free of nuclear weapons and said it was one of the first three countries to sign and ratify the TPNW. Period fit: useful fallback for Chapter 1B context, even though Thailand is non-nuclear. Attribution: official, favorable, state position. Limitations: reflects national diplomacy, not ruler conduct. Contrary points: because Thailand is non-nuclear, this is mostly negative/contextual evidence rather than active capability evidence.

**Compact Event Map**
- **February 10, 2022**: Prayut publicly frames APEC 2022 and the recovery agenda.
- **July 23, 2022**: He survives a parliamentary censure vote.
- **August 24, 2022**: Constitutional Court suspends him from active duties.
- **September 30, 2022**: Court rules he has not exceeded the term limit and may stay.
- **November 2022**: APEC summit period becomes a major flashpoint for protest repression.
- **Late 2022**: Economic recovery is real but still constrained by inflation, weaker external demand, and poverty risk.

**Chapter Source Plan**
- **1B**: Use the MFA TPNW statement as the main 2022 non-nuclear context source; if you need a broader technical baseline, add FAS/NTI only as a fallback.
- **2B**: The local UCDP/SIPRI priors are enough for country-year conflict and military-spend context; add Reuters/AP only if ruler attribution or event narrative is needed.
- **3B**: Use HRW, Prachatai, Thai PBS, and the local prior set for rights, protest, detention, and repression narratives.
- **4B**: Use Thai PBS, the Constitutional Court, and press-freedom/protest sources to anchor political-freedom constraints and institutional limits.
- **5B / 6B**: Use the local economic and welfare priors first; IMF and World Bank are the best narrative complements for macro conditions and inherited constraints.
- **7B**: Use the parliament record, the Constitutional Court, and rights/corruption reporting to separate institutional corruption context from personal-integrity claims.
- **8B**: Use the parliament record, court decisions, IMF/World Bank, and government statements to frame governance capacity without overstating ruler credit.
